Section Name:ELECTION OF PRESIDENT
Title:ELECTION OF PRESIDENT (Motion)
MPs Speaking:Encik Sidek Bin Saniff (Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education); Mr Lee Kuan Yew (Prime Minister); Mr Tang Guan Seng (Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs); Dr Aline K. Wong; Dr Lee Siew-Choh; Mr Chiam See Tong; Mr K. Shanmugam; Mr Abdullah Tarmugi (Mr Deputy Speaker);


Column: 489

[Mr Deputy Speaker (Mr Abdullah Tarmugi) in the Chair]

ELECTION OF PRESIDENT



    The Prime Minister: Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I beg to move the motion* standing in my name on the Order Paper.
*The motion reads as follows:--

    That this Parliament, in accordance with Article 17 of the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore, elects Mr Wee Kim Wee as President of the Republic of Singapore for a further term of four years to commence immediately after the expiry of his present term of office.


    Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, when I moved the motion to elect Mr Wee Kim Wee as President, four years ago on 30 August 1985, he was not well-known to Singaporeans. I said then:

    "What Singapore needs in a President is a man of integrity and dignity. He is without affectations. His easy manner and his understanding of people will make him a good Head of State."

    Sir, today Wee Kim Wee needs no introduction. Most Singaporeans have seen and many have met their President and like him. They speak of him with affection.

Column: 490

He has time and a kind word for everybody. He is an outgoing person who has reached out to a wide range of people by taking an active interest in community activities and community organizations. He exudes warmth and genuine concern for friends and people he meets. And he does not distinguish between VIPs and ordinary Singaporeans.

    Without fanfare he regularly visits welfare homes for the disabled and the aged. He attends and supports many fund-raising functions organized by them, and to show appreciation for their work and to encourage them, he invites the donors, the helpers, the volunteers to receptions at the Istana. He has also visited many Government ministries and departments showing interest in the work and concern for the welfare of the staff.

Column: 491



    I asked the President how he would sum up the last four years if he had to write it up for his resume. He replied:

    "To single out the greatest satisfaction I have derived from my office is easy. It has been the opportunity to meet people - foreigners and Singaporeans, from visiting foreign Heads of States and governments and other dignitaries, to my Singaporean compatriots from all walks of life. For me, this aspect alone outweighs all other considerations."

    He added:

    "I am deeply grateful for the moral support and encouragement shown to me by all quarters, including the people of Singapore, especially during my recent bout of illness."

    Sir, he has lost some weight since his two operations in January and February this year. But he has recovered a large measure of his enthusiasm, his cheerfulness and his vitality.

    I ask the House to support this motion for his re-election.

    Question proposed.

    The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Encik Sidek bin Saniff)(In Malay): Mr Deputy Speaker, I rise in support of the motion moved by the Hon. Prime Minister to elect Mr Wee Kim Wee as President of the Republic of Singapore for a second term of office.

    Mr Deputy Speaker, two things impressed me most when the Prime Minister moved the same motion four years ago on the 30th August 1985. And these words still hold true today. First, he referred to the competence of our President who was able to give clear descriptions or reports of what he observed when he was a High Commissioner then. I quote:

    (In English): "His despatches in analyzing the situation always got him to the heart of the matter."

    (In Malay): The second thing that impressed me then was how Singapore needed someone of integrity and honour. In addition, the Prime Minister made a point about his unassuming character and the unique understanding and compassion he showed to people. I quote the Prime Minister:

    (In English):

Column: 492



    "What Singapore needs in a President is a man of integrity and dignity. He is without affectations. His easy manner and understanding of people will make him a good Head of State."
(In Malay)


    After four years having him as President, we can see for ourselves how well the description fits the character of our President. In point of fact, this has always been his character. The assumption of office has only brought it into the highlight. In my view, two vital aspects have now emerged. First, the sharpness of his mind and the depth of his understanding of life has enabled him to maintain the dignity of the high office of President that he holds. Indeed, the dignity of this high office has been reinforced and it has gained even more respect and higher esteem. Second, his concern for the people, for people of all strata and of all walks of life, from the healthy to the feeble, from the common man to men of position, these have made him into someone in whom they could place love, at the very least place a little bit of love. And what is most important is that he served a people of a variety of races and religions: Chinese, Malays, Indians, Eurasians, and others, who are Buddhists, Muslims, Christians, Hindus, etc, and he performs this task without there existing or without him creating any class barrier, much less a dividing wall. In this way, solidarity is forged or welded. To him, position does not blind the eye, rank does not corrode the heart, his feet always stand firmly on the ground. This has brought him ever higher respect and adulation from the people. His unassuming character and his highly sympathetic and tolerant nature should be emulated by the people. He represents all of us and he represents the whole Singapore society.

    This has led me to conclude that in the midst of our society exists a President whose heart lies in the people. He embodies the meaning caputured by the concept "a People's President". Thus he deserve to be called a "People's President". His election as President of the Republic of Singapore is a fitting one.

    On that note, I fully support the motion moved by the Hon. Prime Minister.
